neurips-2023-megabyte-predicting-million.tldr: MEGABYTE combines local and global transformers to model million-byte sequences without tokenization.
paragraphs: Autoregressive Transformers handle short sequences well but become costly on long raw inputs such as books, audio, and high-resolution images. MEGABYTE introduces a multiscale decoder that supports end-to-end differentiable modeling of sequences longer than one million bytes.

The architecture splits a sequence into patches, applies a local submodel within each patch, and uses a global model across patches. This yields subquadratic attention, permits larger feedforward layers at a given compute budget, and improves parallelism during decoding.

Experiments show byte-level language modeling competitive with subword models on long contexts, state-of-the-art ImageNet density estimation, and audio modeling from raw files. The abstract does not give individual scores or speedups. Together, the demonstrations support tokenization-free autoregressive modeling at scale across these data types, rather than implying one model setting is automatically best for every long-sequence application.

neurips-2023-multi-agent-first-order-con.tldr: MAFOCOPS uses first-order constrained updates to balance multi-agent reward and safety requirements.
paragraphs: Multi-agent reinforcement learning must coordinate performance while potentially limiting unsafe behavior. MAFOCOPS formulates these goals as constrained policy optimization, using experience generated by the agents’ current policies to guide their next update.

The algorithm first solves for an update in a nonparametric policy space and then projects that result into the parameterized policy space used by the learned model. Its first-order structure is intended to make implementation easier than methods requiring more elaborate optimization machinery.

The authors provide an approximate upper bound on worst-case constraint violation and evaluate several safe multi-agent benchmarks. Results show strong performance while satisfying the tested safety constraints. The abstract does not provide exact violation bounds or benchmark values. Its safety claim belongs to the specified constraints and analysis, rather than guaranteeing absence of every harmful action in arbitrary real-world multi-agent deployments.

neurips-2023-non-asymptotic-analysis-of-.tldr: A UCB-based Top Two rule gains finite-confidence sample-complexity guarantees for best-arm identification.
paragraphs: Top Two bandit algorithms choose the next sample from a leader and a challenger, offering simple procedures with strong empirical behavior. Earlier guarantees for fixed-confidence best-arm identification applied mainly as the allowed error probability approached zero. This paper studies performance at arbitrary error levels.

The authors derive a nonasymptotic upper bound on the expected samples required by a Top Two algorithm. Their analysis identifies sufficient properties for a regret-minimization algorithm to select the leader, and shows that the upper-confidence-bound algorithm satisfies those properties.

The resulting UCB-based Top Two method combines the finite-confidence guarantee with competitive experimental performance. The abstract does not give the explicit bound or numerical comparisons. The contribution is a stronger theoretical foundation for a practical sampling pattern, rather than replacing best-arm identification with regret minimization or claiming every possible leader rule enjoys the same guarantee.

neurips-2023-objaverse-xl-a-universe-of-.tldr: Objaverse-XL expands 3D training data to over ten million deduplicated objects.
paragraphs: Large datasets have accelerated language and two-dimensional vision, while three-dimensional learning has faced data-collection barriers. Objaverse-XL addresses that bottleneck with more than ten million deduplicated three-dimensional objects gathered from diverse sources.

The collection includes manually designed assets, photogrammetry scans of landmarks and everyday items, and professional scans of historical and antique artifacts. This range is intended to supply both greater scale and broader coverage than smaller existing collections.

The authors demonstrate benefits by training Zero123 for novel-view synthesis using over 100 million multiview rendered images, obtaining strong zero-shot generalization. The abstract does not give numerical benchmark gains or claim uniform quality across all source objects. Its central contribution is a large shared data resource, accompanied by an experiment showing how its scale can improve a specific three-dimensional vision capability.

neurips-2023-offline-imitation-learning-.tldr: OILCA uses identifiable latent modeling to augment scarce expert demonstrations with counterfactual samples.
paragraphs: Offline imitation learning must learn from fixed data without collecting additional interactions. When demonstrations are mostly suboptimal and rewards are absent, an agent can memorize poor behavior and generalize badly. OILCA addresses that problem through counterfactual data augmentation.

The framework uses an identifiable variational autoencoder to generate samples for augmenting expert data. The authors theoretically analyze how the generated data affect learning and generalization, linking the augmentation procedure to a structured latent model rather than treating arbitrary synthetic trajectories as expert behavior.

Experiments show substantial improvements over several baselines on DeepMind Control for in-distribution performance and CausalWorld for out-of-distribution generalization. The abstract does not specify identification assumptions or numerical gains. Its evidence supports the proposed augmentation under the evaluated conditions, rather than establishing that any suboptimal offline dataset can reveal an optimal policy without additional assumptions.

neurips-2023-oracle-complexity-of-single.tldr: A single-loop switching subgradient method gains complexity guarantees for weakly convex constrained problems.
paragraphs: The switching subgradient method is an intuitive first-order approach to constrained optimization, but its oracle complexity had been understood only for convex problems. This paper analyzes objectives that are weakly convex, with constraints that may be either convex or weakly convex.

The authors derive separate results for the two constraint settings, targeting a nearly stationary point. The method can handle nonsmooth problems while retaining a single-loop implementation, avoiding the need to choose and tune an inner-iteration count as in double-loop alternatives.

The resulting complexity matches existing approaches in the studied settings. The abstract does not state the exact oracle bounds or report experiments. The theoretical target is approximate stationarity in a nonconvex constrained problem, not a global optimum. The contribution makes a simple established algorithm more broadly justified without removing the assumptions that define the weakly convex problem class.

neurips-2023-p-flow-a-fast-and-data-effi.tldr: P-Flow synthesizes a prompted speaker’s voice with continuous representations and a fast flow-matching decoder.
paragraphs: Zero-shot text-to-speech systems can require large training datasets and slow autoregressive generation. P-Flow uses a speech prompt for speaker adaptation while generating continuous mel representations, avoiding reliance on a pretrained neural codec representation.

A speech-prompted text encoder combines text and reference speech into a speaker-conditional representation. A flow-matching decoder then produces personalized speech faster than real time. The system is trained on LibriTTS rather than the much larger collections used by the compared large-scale codec language models.

The authors report comparable speaker similarity with two orders of magnitude less training data and more than 20x faster sampling. Human evaluations favor its naturalness and speaker similarity, with improved pronunciation over recent alternatives. The abstract does not give absolute latency or evaluation scores, so these efficiency and quality claims remain comparisons within the reported experimental setups.

neurips-2023-payoff-based-learning-with-.tldr: Minimal-feedback matrix multiplicative weights can learn equilibria in quantum and semidefinite games.
paragraphs: Quantum games have a continuous space of pure states, making ordinary finite-game payoff-estimation tricks unsuitable. This paper studies learning when players observe only scalar payoffs rather than full game information or each other’s chosen states.

The proposed minimal-information matrix multiplicative weights methods, called 3MW, use a zeroth-order gradient sampler adapted to semidefinite geometry. With deterministic payoff feedback, the method retains an O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence rate in quantum min-max games, matching the full-information matrix-multiplicative-weights rate.

With only a random realization of the payoff observable, the rate becomes O(T^(-1/4)). Beyond zero-sum games, a regularized variant converges locally with high probability to equilibria meeting a first-order stability condition. The guarantees differ by feedback and game class; the abstract does not imply global convergence to every equilibrium in arbitrary general-sum quantum games.

neurips-2023-robust-low-rank-training-vi.tldr: Approximate orthonormal constraints improve the robustness of low-rank neural-network training.
paragraphs: Low-rank weight factorizations can reduce neural-network training and inference costs, but may weaken resistance to adversarial perturbations. This paper models robustness through network conditioning and links the loss of robustness to growing singular values in low-rank weight matrices.

The proposed training algorithm keeps weights on a low-rank matrix manifold while enforcing approximate orthonormal constraints. The intention is to retain computational savings without allowing poor conditioning to undermine the model’s sensitivity to input perturbations.

Numerical experiments support improved robustness without sacrificing accuracy. An approximation theorem shows that the computed low-rank network approximates the ideal full model when a sufficiently strong low-rank subnetwork exists. That existence condition is essential: the theorem does not promise that every full model admits an equally capable compressed version. The abstract gives no specific compression ratios, attack budgets, or numerical accuracy results.

neurips-2023-smooth-flipping-probability.tldr: Smooth sign-flipping probabilities improve the utility of private random-projection representations.
paragraphs: Random projections can compress feature vectors, but adding differential privacy often reduces downstream usefulness. This paper develops private random-projection and sign-random-projection methods that exploit how rarely a small input change flips the sign of a random projection.

The authors improve a previous random-projection approach using the optimal Gaussian mechanism and introduce smooth flipping probability for sign-based algorithms. This design aims to provide better utility than standard randomized response by using the robustness of the underlying projection.

Retrieval and classification experiments find DP-SignOPORP generally best among the presented alternatives. Because privacy is applied to the original feature representation, downstream processing inherits the corresponding protection. The abstract does not specify privacy-budget values or numerical gains. Its suggestion of wider industrial adoption is a prospective implication, while the demonstrated result is improved utility in the evaluated private-representation methods.

neurips-2023-styletts-2-towards-human-le.tldr: StyleTTS 2 combines latent style diffusion with speech-model adversarial training for natural speech synthesis.
paragraphs: Text-to-speech must choose expressive speaking characteristics as well as pronounce the words. StyleTTS 2 represents style as a latent random variable generated by diffusion, allowing it to select a suitable style from text without requiring reference speech.

The model also uses pretrained speech language models, including WavLM, as discriminators. A differentiable duration-modeling component enables end-to-end adversarial training, with the goal of improving perceived speech naturalness while keeping latent diffusion efficient.

Native-English-speaker judgments rate the system above human recordings on LJSpeech and comparable to them on VCTK. Trained on LibriTTS, it also outperforms earlier publicly available models for zero-shot speaker adaptation. These human-level claims refer to particular perceptual evaluations and datasets; they do not establish superiority to human speech in all conditions. The abstract provides no listener counts or numerical rating scales.

neurips-2023-the-geometry-of-hidden-repr.tldr: Transformer representation geometry can identify intermediate layers with useful semantic information.
paragraphs: Each Transformer layer changes the geometry of its hidden representations. This paper studies intrinsic dimension and neighbor composition to understand how semantic structure develops through models trained on different data, especially protein sequences and image-reconstruction tasks.

The authors observe a recurring pattern: dimensionality first expands, then contracts substantially in intermediate layers, and later remains roughly stable or develops a smaller second peak. Semantic information is strongest around the end of the first peak, with useful representations associated with a relative minimum in the dimension profile.

These observations motivate an unsupervised strategy for selecting intermediate layers for downstream learning. The abstract reports consistency across many models and datasets but supplies no quantitative selection gains. The result is an empirical geometric diagnostic, rather than a proof that the final layer is always inferior or that one universal layer index contains the most meaning.

neurips-2023-undirected-probabilistic-mo.tldr: An energy-based tensor model learns flexible joint structure without choosing a fixed directed generative form.
paragraphs: Tensor decomposition analyzes data with multiple axes, but traditional models require structural or distributional assumptions that may be difficult to choose. This paper uses an undirected energy-based model to represent the joint distribution of tensor entries and latent factors more flexibly.

Neural networks parameterize the joint energy, allowing underlying structure and distributions to be learned from data. The energy design accommodates both static tensors and dynamic tensors with timestamps. Training is difficult because latent factors and an unnormalized distribution create two sources of intractability.

The authors address this with a variational upper bound on a conditional noise-contrastive estimation objective, learning to distinguish observed data from conditional noise. Synthetic and real-world experiments show advantages over alternatives. The abstract does not quantify the gains, and the flexible model still embodies architectural choices; it should not be interpreted as learning without any inductive assumptions whatsoever.

neurips-2023-unicontrol-a-unified-diffus.tldr: UniControl unifies multiple spatially controlled image-generation tasks in one diffusion model.
paragraphs: Language prompts are useful for image generation but do not precisely specify spatial or geometric structure. UniControl combines language with diverse visual conditions so a single model can handle multiple condition-to-image tasks while retaining text control over style and context.

The method augments a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model with a task-aware HyperNet that modulates it for different conditioning tasks. Visual conditions chiefly guide structure, while language provides complementary direction. Training spans nine distinct condition-to-image tasks.

The authors report strong zero-shot generation with unseen visual conditions and frequent improvements over similarly sized single-task controlled models. The abstract does not provide benchmark scores or a measured pixel-level error guarantee. Its contribution is broad control within one shared model, with comparative evidence that combining conditioning tasks need not sacrifice the quality achieved by separate specialized systems.

neurips-2023-zero-one-laws-of-graph-neur.tldr: Certain graph neural classifiers approach deterministic outputs on growing Erdős–Rényi graphs.
paragraphs: Graph neural networks may behave differently as graph size grows far beyond training examples. This paper studies that question theoretically by examining classifiers on increasingly large graphs sampled from the Erdős–Rényi random-graph model.

Under mild assumptions, the probability that a graph is assigned a particular output approaches either zero or one for the studied class of networks. This class includes the popular graph convolutional network architecture. The authors interpret the resulting zero-one laws as limits on representation and extrapolation capacity.

Experiments verify the predicted asymptotic behavior and find it visible even on relatively small graphs. The abstract does not specify the assumptions or finite-size thresholds. The result concerns particular architectures and random-graph distributions; it does not say every graph neural network produces a constant answer on every family of large real-world graphs.

neurips-2024-4-3-phases-of-compute-optim.tldr: A solvable scaling model reveals distinct regimes for allocating compute to neural-network size.
paragraphs: Compute-optimal model size depends on more than a single universal scaling exponent. This paper analyzes a solvable neural model with parameters for data complexity, target complexity, and model size, focusing on a compute-limited regime with effectively unlimited data.

Training uses one-pass stochastic gradient descent with mean-squared loss. The authors derive a representation of the loss curve across all iteration counts whose accuracy improves as parameter count grows. They then optimize model size for a given floating-point-operation budget.

The analysis identifies four phases and three subphases, separated by the relative influence of capacity, optimization noise, and feature embedding. Mathematical proofs and numerical evidence establish the scaling exponents in each regime. These are results for the specified solvable model, not a universal empirical law for every modern architecture. A supplied notebook reproduces selected findings.

neurips-2024-4m-21-an-any-to-any-vision-.tldr: 4M-21 expands a unified any-to-any model across diverse visual, geometric, semantic, and textual modalities.
paragraphs: Multimodal models can only directly support the tasks and input types their training represents. This paper broadens that coverage by training one any-to-any model on many modalities alongside large-scale text and multimodal datasets.

A key step is discrete tokenization across heterogeneous data: images, feature maps, vectors, structured segmentations, human poses, and text-like representations. Training includes outputs from specialist models and modalities such as metadata and color palettes, giving users additional ways to steer generation.

The authors show at least three times as many tasks or modalities as existing models without loss of performance and scale training to three billion parameters. They also study combining knowledge from models trained with different objectives. The abstract does not provide per-task scores, so the contribution is demonstrated breadth and controllability within the tested collection, rather than unrestricted support for every conceivable modality.

neurips-2024-a-bayesian-approach-to-data.tldr: Bayesian inference jointly learns example weights and network parameters for efficient data selection.
paragraphs: Large raw datasets are easy to acquire, but selecting useful training examples is costly. Existing data-point-selection methods often use bilevel optimization, which increases memory and computation and raises issues with minibatch formulations. This paper proposes a Bayesian alternative.

It treats instance-specific weights and neural-network parameters as variables in a joint posterior under a chosen prior and likelihood. Stochastic-gradient Langevin sampling updates both together, with convergence support under minibatching. The update is comparable in form to stochastic gradient descent and more efficient than the compared bilevel methods.

Controlled vision and language experiments establish a proof of concept. The authors also scale to large language models and automatically optimize instruction-tuning data for individual tasks. The abstract gives no numerical resource savings or accuracy gains. Its contribution is a probabilistic formulation and practical joint update rather than a claim that every automatically weighted dataset is optimal.

neurips-2024-acceleration-exists-optimiz.tldr: Order-oracle optimization can achieve acceleration using comparisons instead of numerical objective values.
paragraphs: Some black-box systems reveal only which of two candidates is better, not their objective values. This paper studies an order oracle that supplies such comparisons, potentially with bounded noise, and asks how much optimization performance remains possible.

The authors construct nonaccelerated methods for nonconvex, convex, and strongly convex settings by incorporating comparison access into existing optimization tools. Their guarantees match leading coordinate first-order methods and existing order-oracle methods up to logarithmic factors. They also provide an accelerated algorithm using the order oracle.

A different construction establishes asymptotic convergence with a stochastic order oracle, and numerical experiments illustrate the methods. The abstract does not state all smoothness assumptions or exact complexity rates. The contribution is an expansion of comparison-based optimization guarantees, rather than the assertion that any arbitrary black-box objective can be efficiently optimized from rankings alone.

neurips-2024-acfun-abstract-concrete-fus.tldr: ACFun separates abstract and concrete style cues to stylize a face from one reference image.
paragraphs: Facial stylization must preserve recognizable facial information while changing more than surface color and brushwork. Collecting large datasets for every artistic style is impractical. ACFun addresses this by using only one style image and one input face for each stylization task.

The method contains an Abstract Fusion Module and a Concrete Fusion Module to learn different aspects of style and facial content. A Face and Style Imagery Alignment Loss connects the images in latent space, and the final stylized face is generated directly from noise.

Experiments report stronger facial stylization than competing methods, producing artistic and visually pleasing outputs. The abstract does not provide numerical metrics, user-study details, or quantified identity preservation. Its contribution is a two-part representation and alignment strategy for limited-reference stylization, with reported visual benefits rather than a guarantee that every artistic transformation preserves all identifying facial features.

neurips-2024-active-set-ordering-9cc7042.tldr: Active set ordering studies which expensive evaluations are needed to infer useful rankings.
paragraphs: An expensive black-box function may be useful mainly because it orders candidate inputs. This paper formalizes active set ordering, where the learner selects evaluations to discover those relationships rather than needing uniformly precise predictions of every function value.

The proposed mean-prediction algorithm is analyzed through regret on predicted pairwise orderings. Bayesian optimization appears as a special case because identifying a maximizer requires comparisons, even when exact objective values are not the ultimate goal.

The authors reconstruct the Gaussian-process upper-confidence-bound algorithm from this ordering perspective and draw additional insights from that interpretation. Experiments on synthetic functions and real-world datasets validate the proposed solution. The abstract does not give regret formulas or numerical gains. The contribution is both a general problem formulation and an algorithmic lens connecting ranking-oriented active evaluation with familiar Bayesian-optimization methods.

neurips-2024-all-in-one-image-coding-for.tldr: Multi-Path Aggregation shares image-code features while retaining task-specific information for people and machines.
paragraphs: Image compression serving human viewing and machine analysis faces competing objectives. Separate task-specific encoders and decoders increase parameter and bitrate costs, while one shared representation can weaken individual tasks. Multi-Path Aggregation addresses this tension within an all-in-one coding architecture.

A predictor assigns latent features to paths according to task-dependent importance, sharing useful information while preserving features that need specialized refinement. A two-stage optimization strategy uses feature correlations to reduce multitask degradation. Adapting a task can require augmenting and fine-tuning as little as 1.89% of parameters.

Experiments match state-of-the-art performance across viewing and analysis tasks in both task-specific and multiobjective settings. The same model supports transitions between human- and machine-oriented reconstruction. The abstract does not provide bitrate savings or every task score, so the result supports efficient architectural sharing rather than a universal improvement on all compression objectives simultaneously.

neurips-2024-any2graph-deep-end-to-end-s.tldr: Any2Graph predicts variable-sized graphs with a differentiable, permutation-invariant optimal-transport loss.
paragraphs: Supervised graph prediction requires producing an entire graph from an input, including structure whose node ordering should not matter. Any2Graph proposes a generic end-to-end framework intended to work across different input types rather than relying on a separate formulation for each application.

Its central component is a Partially-Masked Fused Gromov–Wasserstein loss. The loss is designed to be permutation invariant, differentiable, and scalable while handling graphs of different sizes, allowing graph predictions to be trained through a common matching objective.

Experiments outperform existing competitors on a challenging synthetic dataset and real tasks including map construction from satellite images and molecule prediction from fingerprints. The abstract does not supply numerical results or graph-size limits. The contribution is a reusable graph-output learning framework with evidence across these tasks, not proof of equally strong performance for every possible input-to-graph mapping.

neurips-2024-artificial-generational-int.tldr: Balancing social and independent learning lets reinforcement-learning agents accumulate capabilities across generations.
paragraphs: Human cultural progress combines individual discovery with information passed between generations. Reinforcement-learning systems usually optimize within a single lifetime. This paper investigates training setups where agents inherit useful information while retaining opportunities to innovate through independent learning.

The authors construct two forms of generation. Episodic generations accumulate information through in-context learning, while training-time generations accumulate it in model weights. They interpret these as analogues of knowledge and skill accumulation, respectively, building on earlier demonstrations of social learning.

Agents trained with the appropriate balance of imitation and independent learning outperform single-lifetime agents given the same cumulative experience. The abstract does not identify task scores or claim open-ended human-like culture has been achieved. Its evidence is emergent accumulation in the proposed reinforcement-learning models, suggesting a direction for studying longer-term capability growth and formal models of cultural transmission.

neurips-2024-chain-of-thought-reasoning-.tldr: Alternative decoding paths can reveal chain-of-thought reasoning without specialized reasoning prompts.
paragraphs: Chain-of-thought methods often depend on crafted prompts or examples that request intermediate reasoning. This paper instead asks whether such reasoning is already available in pretrained language models but missed by ordinary greedy decoding.

The authors explore top-k alternative tokens during decoding and find that many resulting paths contain chain-of-thought sequences. They also observe that paths containing such reasoning tend to yield higher confidence in the decoded answer, providing a signal for distinguishing them from paths without explicit reasoning.

Experiments across reasoning benchmarks show that this CoT-decoding approach can elicit capabilities obscured by standard greedy generation. The abstract does not give benchmark scores or computational overhead, and higher confidence is reported as a correlation rather than proof of correctness. The contribution is a decoding-based route to reasoning behavior that reduces dependence on specialized chain-of-thought prompt engineering.
